# Dot / Lab

> A library of 20 Canvas 2D dot patterns, eight dynamical systems, and nine loader states for React, licensed under MIT.

Open an animation in the Library to access its Playground. Download .tsx saves a standalone DotField.tsx containing all 20 patterns and the license. Copy component copies the same source with a commented usage example using the current settings. The Code tab's Copy usage button copies only the usage example.

The exported component requires React 18+ and a build setup that supports TSX. It renders in the browser, includes a 'use client' directive, and imports only React. The website separately uses Motion for its mobile menu and thinking-orbs in its footer; the exported component requires neither.

Set a height on the component or its parent. The canvas background is transparent.

```tsx
import { DotField } from './DotField';

<DotField pattern="sphere" color="#baff66" style={{ height: 480 }} />
```

Props and defaults:

- `pattern`: `"sphere"`; select one of the IDs below.
- `color`: `"#baff66"`; any CSS color.
- `speed`: `0.5`; clamped to 0–5. Zero stops animation.
- `paused`: `false`; freezes animation at its current time.
- `density`: `1`; 1,150 dots by default, clamped to 160–2,200 dots.
- `morph`: `false`; animates a transition when the caller changes `pattern`.
- `className`: unset; optional canvas CSS class.
- `style`: unset; optional React styles, including height.

Pattern IDs:

```text
sphere torus wave vortex helix
ripple galaxy cube infinity aurora
dna bloom tunnel orbit terrain
knot rain constellation pulse lattice
```

The component pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, and uses a static frame for reduced-motion preferences. Pattern changes while paused or under reduced motion display the new shape without a transition. The website hero cycles sphere, torus, and wave every six seconds while active; the exported component has no automatic pattern cycle.

Keep the included MIT license notice when redistributing the component.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Hero preview and link to the GitHub repository.
- [Dot patterns](/#collection): Browse the original 20 animations and open the Playground to adjust color, speed, and density.
- [Dynamical systems](/dynamical-systems/): Lorenz, Rössler, Thomas, Hénon, Clifford, Chua, Rucklidge, and Rabinovich–Fabrikant. Includes live equations, parameter controls, current values, pause/step, and standalone TSX export.
- [Dot loaders](/loaders/): Compact state indicators with size examples, motion and appearance controls, and standalone TSX export.

## Dynamical systems exports

The systems playground downloads Attractor.tsx, including the current system, coefficients, appearance, motion settings, and random seed in its default Attractor component. Import Attractor from './Attractor' and render <Attractor style={{ height: 480 }} />. The file includes its renderer, equations, particle noise, and MIT license. React 18+ is its only runtime dependency.

Every particle has an independent base state and advances under the equations. Continuous flows use fixed-step RK4 integration with interpolation for smooth drawing; discrete maps apply the recurrence directly with visual easing between calculated states. Speed changes the number of numerical steps per second. Simulations discard a warm-up transient, stop offscreen or in hidden tabs, and respect reduced motion. Live values represent the tracked particle's exact underlying numerical state; flow readouts show derivatives, and map readouts show the next state.

The fade prop controls independent per-particle opacity cycles (0–1, default 0.7). The drift prop controls gentle camera wandering without altering the equations (0–1, default 0.6). The trails prop controls short motion trails (0–1, default 0.55). Set these to 0 to disable their respective effects. Speed accepts 0–5 and defaults to 0.5. Pause freezes particles, fading, and camera drift together; appearance changes preserve the simulation.

Random motion adds independent wandering offsets to displayed dots without altering the equations or live values. The randomness prop accepts 0–1, default 0 (off). noiseDirection is 'all' (All directions, default) or 'horizontal' (Side to side). noiseSeed defaults to 42; Reseed increments it to generate a different repeatable pattern. Copy/download preserves all three props.

The playground's Show tracking dot checkbox controls showMarker (boolean, default false). Set it to true to display the large marker and its halo without changing particles or live values. Copy/download preserves this setting.

The playground checks coefficient changes before applying them and retains the last working settings if the candidate diverges. Later divergence restores the default coefficients with a notice. Some bounded settings settle into fixed points or repeating orbits. The standalone renderer stops on divergence rather than changing the mathematical system silently.

## Dot loader exports

The loader playground downloads DotLoader.tsx with all states, selected settings, and the MIT license. Import its default export to retain the preset; the named DotLoader export uses the base defaults. The exported client component imports only React and requires React 18+.

State IDs: idle, connecting, listening, searching, retrieving, processing, generating, streaming, complete. Pass state from the application as its operation changes; the component does not perform or detect those operations.

Processing alternates quarter-turns of horizontal and vertical layers. Complete runs a one-shot gather of all 27 dots into the center, holds briefly, reforms the cube, and continues as idle breathing without mutating the caller's state prop. Reduced motion skips to the final cube. The playground includes Replay completion without resetting selected settings.

Defaults: state="processing", size=64 pixels, color="#baff66", speed=0.7, intensity=0.65, spacing=1, dotSize=1, depth=0.65, yaw=-32 degrees, pitch=22 degrees, level=0.5, paused=false. Optional label supplies an accessible name; omit it for a decorative indicator next to descriptive text. className and style are optional.

The listening level is controlled by the caller; no microphone access is included. State transitions retain the mounted component. Pause, zero speed, and reduced-motion preferences freeze animation. The canvas is transparent; preview backgrounds are not exported. The background toggle also selects a readable dot color, which is exported.
